statement: Find the shortest distance between the two lines $\\mathbf{r}=(0,0,0)+s(1,1,0)$ and $\\mathbf{r}=(0,0,1)+t(0,1,1)$, and the points on each line that are closest together.
solution: A general point on the first line is $(s,s,0)$ and on the second is $(0,t,1+t)$. The vector joining them is $(s,\,s-t,\,-1-t)$. For the shortest distance this vector is perpendicular to both direction vectors $(1,1,0)$ and $(0,1,1)$: dot with $(1,1,0)$ gives $s+(s-t)=2s-t=0$, so $t=2s$; dot with $(0,1,1)$ gives $(s-t)+(-1-t)=s-2t-1=0$. Substituting $t=2s$ yields $s-4s-1=0$, so $s=-1/3$ and $t=-2/3$. The closest points are $(-1/3,-1/3,0)$ on the first line and $(0,-2/3,1/3)$ on the second; the joining vector is $(1/3,-1/3,1/3)$ of length $\\sqrt{3}/3=1/\\sqrt{3}$. Hence the shortest distance is $1/\\sqrt{3}$.
hints: Parameterise a point on each line.
Set the joining vector perpendicular to both direction vectors.
Solve for s and t, then compute the distance.
